answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic stake burning per identity: creating n identities requires burning c*n^2 tokens, imposing superlinear cost scaling so attackers face quadratic friction. Validated agents stake tokens locked across an epoch horizon; any attempt to forge consensus triggers slash-and-burn protocols. Identity vouchers require collateral verified through a jade threshold lattice, making mass replication economically ruinous.
